prompt:
Rewrite snippets/spec-sheet-2.liquid so it renders a product specification sheet that copes with null and empty-string inputs. Inputs (all top-level variables): - `title`: string or null. - `specs`: always an array (it may be empty). Each element is an object that always has the three keys `label`, `value` and `unit`. Each of these is a string or null. Normalisation: treat null as an empty string, then strip leading and trailing whitespace from `title` and from every `label`, `value` and `unit`. A value is "blank" if it is empty after stripping. Rules: 1. A spec whose stripped label is blank is skipped entirely. 2. If no spec survives rule 1 (including when `specs` is empty), output nothing at all (an empty string), even if a title is present. 3. Otherwise output `
`. Next comes the title, only if the stripped title is not blank: `

TITLE

`. Then `
`, then one row per surviving spec in the original array order, then `
`. 4. Each row is `
LABEL
DD
`, where DD is: - `
N/A
` if the stripped value is blank. The unit is ignored in this case. - `
VALUE
` if the value is not blank and the stripped unit is blank. - `
VALUE UNIT
` (exactly one space between them) if both are non-blank. 5. TITLE, LABEL, VALUE and UNIT are the stripped texts, HTML-escaped with the core `escape` filter (& becomes &, < becomes <, > becomes >, " becomes "). 6. The output must contain no whitespace or newlines between tags. Use whitespace control so the result is a single line. Output only the specified elements/attributes; escape dynamic text and attributes. Inter-element whitespace, comments and quote style may vary; leaf text is exact. Change only snippets/spec-sheet-2.liquid. Do not suppress checks or hardcode case values. All input keys are present.
